signals.title: NOK/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hormuz Supply Shock
signals.text: Weekend escalation in the Strait of Hormuz after a tanker ignited on a naval mine combines with WTI crude settling up 2.61% at $99.0/bbl to generate strong topside momentum for NOK against USD. The G10 scorecard confirms NOK as the week's leader at +1.374% (n=2) versus USD as the primary laggard at -0.607% (n=9), opening a 1.981% performance spread that easily clears the critical threshold. With USD/NOK closing Friday at 9.4140 below its 20, 50, and 200-day SMAs, widening energy supply disruption drives acute outperformance into the Asia open. Trade bias: Bullish NOK against USD into the Sydney open. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo market reopen following Strait of Hormuz naval mine strike. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Persian Gulf pushing WTI back below $96.0/bbl.
evidence: Strait of Hormuz tanker strike headline

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme Speculative Short Overhang Ahead of CPI
signals.text: CAD COT leveraged funds net short sits at -89.7k contracts (16.0% long, 15th percentile, z = -1.32), creating severe short-squeeze vulnerability if domestic inflation surprises higher. USD/CAD closed Friday at 1.4137 beneath its 20-day SMA of 1.4188, while retail positioning shows an extreme 87% short skew that sets up sharp counter-trend volatility. Elevated crude prices at $99.0/bbl provide baseline support to CAD, but the heavy speculative short base limits fresh CAD downside prior to official data releases. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD on positioning squeeze risk. Catalyst: Canada CPI release at 12:30 UTC on Monday. Risk: Canada Core CPI missing consensus expectations below 2.1% YoY.
evidence: CAD COT LF net: -89,659 (16.0% long, pctl 15)

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Euro Shorts vs Widening OIS Carry Drag
signals.text: EUR COT leveraged funds net short stands at -92.8k contracts (33.3% long, 4th percentile, z = -1.78), establishing high short-covering vulnerability after Friday's close at 1.1242. Fed rate hike expectations softened following Chair Powell's neutral posture, softening dollar momentum despite the +145bp OIS carry advantage currently favoring USD. With EUR/USD trading below all key daily moving averages (20, 50, and 200-day SMAs), any stabilization in European cross-asset sentiment threatens to force an aggressive positioning unwind. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD on speculative short squeeze into the open. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo session open followed by ECB meeting on 29 Oct. Risk: US 2Y yield advancing beyond 4.85% to re-ignite broad dollar demand.
evidence: EUR COT LF net: -92,833 (33.3% long, pctl 4, z = -1.78)

signals.title: AUD/USD — Stretched Speculative Longs Face Commodity Divergence
signals.text: AUD COT leveraged funds net long stands elevated at +45.0k contracts (67.9% long), leaving the pair exposed to liquidation after closing Friday at 0.6949 below its 20, 50, and 200-day SMAs. A notable correlation divergence between AUD/USD and gold (corr +0.452 vs norm +0.563, z = -1.43σ) signals weakening demand for commodity beta amid rising Middle East tensions. Although the AONIA-SOFR OIS spread retains a +71bp carry advantage for the Australian dollar, net positioning overhang limits immediate upside participation. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD on long-liquidation risk. Catalyst: Sydney market open and RBA meeting on 3 Nov. Risk: Broad commodity index surge lifting AUD above the 20-day SMA at 0.6992.
